title: DATEDIF: days, months or years between

screens.prompt: The dates in B and C are serials, not text: put the complete years Ada has served into D2, counting only full years.

hints.syntax: DATEDIF reads left to right: start, then end, then the unit in quotes: =DATEDIF(B2,C2,"Y").
hints.func-datedif: DATEDIF is the one that answers in whole units; subtracting two serials answers in days, so read it off C2 and B2 instead.
hints.require-ref: Point at B2 and C2 rather than typing the two serials into the call.
hints.value: 44562 is 1 January 2022 and 45352 is 1 March 2024, so two full years have passed and the two months since are not counted.
hints.error: DATEDIF answers #NUM! for a unit it does not know, or when the start date falls after the end date.

reject.why: the days between, which is not the same question as the years served
no unit, so DATEDIF has nothing to answer in — days, months and years are three different answers
the serials typed in, so a corrected review date never reaches the answer
the months between, 26, rather than the complete years
the days between, 790 — a count of days is not a count of years
start and end swapped, so DATEDIF answers #NUM!
Q is not a unit DATEDIF knows, so the answer is #NUM!
the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs

screens.prompt: Same person, different question: put the complete months since Grace started into D2.

hints.syntax: Same three arguments, a different unit: =DATEDIF(B2,C2,"M").
hints.func-datedif: DATEDIF with the month unit, not a subtraction and not DAYS.
hints.require-ref: Read the two serials from B2 and C2.
hints.value: 44197 is 1 January 2021, so three whole years is 36 months and January to March 2024 adds the other two.
hints.error: A unit DATEDIF does not know comes back as #NUM!, so a typo in the quotes is a visible failure rather than a wrong number.

reject.why: the days between, 1155, rather than the complete months
no unit at all, so DATEDIF cannot answer
the serials typed in, so the answer stops following the row
three whole years — the month unit counts thirty-eight
the months left over after whole years, which is 2, not the total since starting
L is not a unit DATEDIF knows, so the cell fills with #NUM!
the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs

docs.explain: Subtracting one date from another answers in days and nothing else. DATEDIF answers in whichever unit you name. It is also the only function that answers in the leftovers: complete years between two dates, complete months, days left over after those years, months left over after them. It takes a start date, an end date, and a unit written as text in quotes. Y, M and D give whole years, months and days, and YM, MD, YD give the remainders. The word complete is the whole point. From 1 January 2022 to 1 March 2024 nobody has served three years yet, so Y answers 2, and a birthday that has not arrived is not a year of service. Nothing in the arguments says which unit you meant, so a wrong unit is a plausible number rather than an error. 26 is the right answer to a different question, which is why it grades as a wrong answer here instead of a typo. DATEDIF is old enough that Excel still hides it from the function list. It answers #NUM! when the unit is unknown or the start date falls after the end, so both failures are at least loud.

errors.text: The unit in quotes is not one DATEDIF knows: Y, M, D, YM, MD and YD are the whole list.
The start date falls after the end date, so there is no positive difference to report.
A date argument was text that does not read as a date, so DATEDIF has no serial to work from.

docs.atWork: A staff review sheet that reports years of service without dividing a day count by 365. The question the HR export asks is complete years, and DATEDIF is the only function that answers it.
docs.outcome: Ask for the difference between two dates in whole years, months or days, and get the leftovers when you want them too.
docs.dataset: Two employees, their start dates and one review date

seo.title: DATEDIF in Excel: days, months or years
seo.description: DATEDIF answers in the unit you name, leftovers included, so Y gives complete years and YM the months after them. A wrong unit returns a plausible number.
